words.ex: He uses a computer terminal to log in.
words.ex_cn: 他使用计算机终端登录。
words.en: A device with a screen and keyboard for interacting with a computer, often in a public or shared setting.

words.ex: He is the author of this book.
words.ex_cn: 他是这本书的作者。
words.en: An author is a person who writes books, stories, or articles, especially as a job.

words.ex: He is a writer who loves to write stories.
words.ex_cn: 他是一位喜欢写故事的作家。
words.en: A writer is a person who writes books, stories, or articles as a job or regular occupation.

words.ex: The publisher released a new book last month.
words.ex_cn: 出版者上个月发布了一本新书。
words.en: A publisher is a person or company that prepares and issues books, journals, or music for sale.

words.ex: The publication of his book was delayed.
words.ex_cn: 他的书的出版被推迟了。
words.en: The act of making something available to the public, especially a book, magazine, or newspaper.

words.tr:
n. 新闻界；出版社；
v. 按；压；
words.ex: The press reported the news quickly.
words.ex_cn: 新闻界迅速报道了这则新闻。
words.en: To press something is to push it firmly, often with your fingers or hand, in order to operate a device or machine, or to make something flat or smooth. It can also mean to urge someone to do something or to make a strong demand for something.

words.ex: The president held a press conference yesterday.
words.ex_cn: 总统昨天召开了新闻发布会。
words.en: A press conference is a meeting organized for the purposes of distributing information to the media and answering questions from reporters.

words.tr: phrase. 牛津大学出版社（隶属于牛津大学的世界知名学术与教材出版机构）
words.ex: He bought a book from Oxford University Press.
words.ex_cn: 他从牛津大学出版社买了一本书。
words.en: Oxford University Press is a department of the University of Oxford, and it is the largest university press in the world by the number of publications.

words.ex: He bought a book from Cambridge University Press.
words.ex_cn: 他从剑桥大学出版社买了一本书。
words.en: Cambridge University Press is the publishing business of the University of Cambridge, one of the world's leading academic publishers.

words.ex: He uses his library card to borrow books.
words.ex_cn: 他用他的借书证借书。
words.en: A library card is a card issued by a library to individuals, entitling them to borrow books and other materials.

words.ex: He showed his admission card to borrow a book.
words.ex_cn: 他出示了他的借书证来借书。
words.en: A ticket or pass that allows someone to enter a place or event.

words.ex: He showed his passport at the airport.
words.ex_cn: 他在机场出示了他的护照。
words.en: A passport is an official document that identifies you as a citizen of a particular country and gives you the right to travel to and from that country.

words.ex: He took a passport photo at the studio.
words.ex_cn: 他在照相馆拍了一张护照照片。
words.en: A photograph that is required for official documents such as passports.

words.ex: He got his driving licence last month.
words.ex_cn: 他上个月拿到了驾照。
words.en: A driving licence is an official document permitting a specific individual to operate one or more types of motorized vehicles on public roads.

words.ex: He got his driving license last week.
words.ex_cn: 他上周拿到了驾照。
words.en: A driving license is an official document which shows that you have passed the necessary tests and are allowed to drive a vehicle.

words.ex: He checked his bank statement last night.
words.ex_cn: 他昨晚查看了他的银行对账单。
words.en: A bank statement is a document that shows all the transactions that have occurred in a bank account over a specific period of time, usually a month.

words.ex: He shows his student card to get a discount.
words.ex_cn: 他出示学生证来获得折扣。
words.en: A card issued by an educational institution to a student, which is used to identify the student and may provide access to certain facilities or services.

words.ex: He wrote his name on the call slip.
words.ex_cn: 他在借书单上写了名字。
words.en: A call slip is a form used in libraries to request a book or other material that is kept in closed stacks.

words.tr: n. 清单；检查表；备忘录；目录册；
words.ex: He made a checklist for his trip.
words.ex_cn: 他为旅行列了一份清单。
words.en: A checklist is a list of items required, things to be done, or points to be considered, used as a reminder.

words.ex: The index of 2 in 2^3 is 3.
words.ex_cn: 2^3 中 2 的指数是 3。
words.en: An index is a system by which changes in the value of something and the rate at which it changes can be recorded, measured, or interpreted.

words.ex: He added the bibliography at the end of his report.
words.ex_cn: 他在报告末尾添加了参考书目。
words.en: A bibliography is a list of the books and articles that have been used by someone when writing a particular book or article.

words.tr: adj. 可获得的；有空的；可用的；
words.ex: The books are available in the library.
words.ex_cn: 这些书在图书馆里可以借到。
words.en: If something is available, it is able to be used or obtained.

words.tr: phrase. 在架子上；搁置的；被弃置的；无人过问的（尤指因过时或不再流行）
words.ex: She's been on the shelf since her last relationship ended.
words.ex_cn: 自从上次恋情结束后，她就一直单身。
words.en: If something is on the shelf, it is not being used or is not available for use at the present time.

words.ex: The bank gave a loan to the student.
words.ex_cn: 银行向学生提供了一笔贷款。
words.en: A loan is a sum of money that you borrow.

words.ex: The book is out on loan to a student.
words.ex_cn: 这本书借给了一名学生。
words.en: If something is out on loan, it has been lent to someone and is not currently available.

words.tr: phrase. 借阅期；贷款期限；借出期间
words.ex: The loan period for books is two weeks.
words.ex_cn: 书籍的借阅期是两周。
words.en: The duration for which something, especially a book from a library, is borrowed.

words.ex: The circulation of blood keeps us alive.
words.ex_cn: 血液的循环让我们活着。
words.en: The movement of something such as money or goods from place to place or from person to person; the number of copies of a newspaper or magazine that are sold.

words.tr: phrase. 在流通中被保留的；处于流通但受限制的
words.ex: The coins are reserved in circulation for collectors.
words.ex_cn: 这些硬币被保留用于收藏者流通。
words.en: Kept aside or retained within the flow or distribution of something, especially money or goods.

words.tr: phrase. 不在流通的；不再活跃的；不参与社交活动的
words.ex: That coin is out of circulation now.
words.ex_cn: 那枚硬币现在不再流通了。
words.en: If something is out of circulation, it is no longer available or no longer being used or seen in public.

words.ex: This document is not for circulation.
words.ex_cn: 这份文件不得外传。
words.en: This term is used to denote items, especially currency or documents, that are not intended for general distribution or use among the public.

words.tr:
n. 保护区；储备；保留；
v. 预订；
words.ex: The wildlife reserve is home to many endangered animals.
words.ex_cn: 这个自然保护区是许多濒危动物的家园。
words.en: If you reserve something such as a table, ticket, or magazine, you arrange for it to be kept for you and not given to anyone else.

words.tr: phrase. 保留区；预留部分；图书馆藏书保留区（仅供馆内阅览不外借的区域）
words.ex: He reserved a seat in the reserve section.
words.ex_cn: 他预订了预留区域的一个座位。
words.en: A designated area in a library where books are kept for specific use or borrowing.

words.ex: The book is in the closed reserve at the library.
words.ex_cn: 这本书在图书馆的闭架阅览区。
words.en: A state of being reserved or restrained, often due to shyness or caution.

words.ex: We booked in advance to get good seats.
words.ex_cn: 我们提前预订了座位，以便得到好位置。
words.en: To arrange for something to be reserved or secured at a time before it is needed.

words.ex: We checked out of the hotel after paying the bill.
words.ex_cn: 我们付完账后离开了酒店。
words.en: To check out means to leave a hotel after paying your bill, or to examine something or someone in order to be certain that everything is correct, safe, or satisfactory.

words.ex: He will renew his passport next week.
words.ex_cn: 他下周会更新他的护照。
words.en: To renew something means to begin it again or to make it new again.

words.tr: phrase. 续借这本书；延长这本书的借阅期限
words.ex: He will renew the book tomorrow.
words.ex_cn: 他明天要续借这本书。
words.en: To extend the loan period of a book borrowed from a library.

words.ex: The renewal of the contract took one week.
words.ex_cn: 合同的更新花了一周时间。
words.en: The act of making something valid for a further period of time after it has expired or been canceled.

words.tr:
n. 请求；要求的事；
v. 要求；请求；
words.ex: He made a request for help.
words.ex_cn: 他提出了一个帮助的请求。
words.en: If you request something, you ask for it politely or formally.

words.ex: This job requires patience.
words.ex_cn: 这份工作需要耐心。
words.en: If you require something, you need it or want it.

words.tr:
v. 回忆起；召回；
n. 记忆力；
words.ex: I recall my first day at school.
words.ex_cn: 我想起了我上学的第一天。
words.en: If you recall something, you remember it and tell others about it.

words.tr: phrase. 召回系统；回忆系统；检索系统
words.ex: The company activated the recall system for defective toys.
words.ex_cn: 公司启动了缺陷玩具的召回系统。
words.en: A method or process for retrieving information or items from a collection.

words.tr:
n. 返回；归还；
v. 返回；归还；
words.ex: The return of the train was delayed.
words.ex_cn: 火车的返回被推迟了。
words.en: To go or come back to a place or person. To give, send, or put something back to its original place or condition.

words.ex: Please return the book in time.
words.ex_cn: 请及时归还这本书。
words.en: To come or go back to a place or person at a suitable or expected time.

words.tr: phrase. 在7个工作日内返回；须在7个工作日内归还
words.ex: You can return the item within 7 working days.
words.ex_cn: 你可以在7个工作日内退货。
words.en: To send something back or come back within a week and a half (7 working days).

words.tr: adj. 应给的；预期的；到期的；
words.ex: The payment is due tomorrow.
words.ex_cn: 这笔款项明天应给。
words.en: If something is due at a particular time, it is expected to happen or be done at that time.

words.tr: phrase. 到期日；截止日期；预产期
words.ex: The due date for the homework is Friday.
words.ex_cn: 作业的截止日期是星期五。
words.en: The date by which something is expected to happen or be completed.

words.ex: The milk's expiry date is tomorrow.
words.ex_cn: 这瓶牛奶的保质期是明天。
words.en: The date on which something, especially a contract or agreement, comes to an end or ceases to be valid.

words.tr: phrase. 终止日期；借书期限
words.ex: The date of expiry is tomorrow.
words.ex_cn: 到期日期是明天。
words.en: The date on which something, especially a contract, agreement, or product, is no longer valid or usable.

words.ex: The book is overdue at the library.
words.ex_cn: 这本书在图书馆逾期了。
words.en: If you say that a change or an event is overdue, you mean that you think it should have happened before now.

words.tr: phrase. 逾期未还的书；超期图书
words.ex: The library charges a fine for every overdue book.
words.ex_cn: 图书馆对每本逾期未还的书收取罚款。
words.en: A book that has not been returned to the library by the due date.

words.tr: phrase. 期限；（图书馆）借书卡
words.ex: The date slip for the project is next Friday.
words.ex_cn: 这个项目的期限是下周五。
words.en: A small piece of paper or a label that indicates a date, often used in libraries to show when a book is due back.

words.tr:
adj. 很好的；晴朗的；健康的；
n. 罚款；
words.ex: She did a fine job on the project.
words.ex_cn: 她在这个项目上做得很好。
words.en: If you say that something is fine, you mean that it is satisfactory or acceptable.

words.tr: phrase. 良好的系统；精密的系统
words.ex: The school has a fine system for helping students learn.
words.ex_cn: 这所学校有一个帮助学生学习的良好系统。
words.en: A system of imposing monetary penalties as a punishment for breaking laws or rules.

words.ex: He must pay the fine for parking illegally.
words.ex_cn: 他必须支付因非法停车而产生的罚款。
words.en: To pay the fine means to give money as a penalty for breaking a law or rule.

words.ex: He went to the clinic for a check-up.
words.ex_cn: 他去诊所做检查。
words.en: A clinic is a place where people receive medical treatment or advice, especially for a particular illness or condition.

words.tr: phrase. 校园诊所；设在大学或学校园区内的医疗诊所
words.ex: He went to the campus clinic for a cold.
words.ex_cn: 他去校医院治感冒。
words.en: A campus clinic is a medical facility located on a university or college campus that provides health services to students and sometimes faculty and staff.

words.ex: He went to the medical centre for a check-up.
words.ex_cn: 他去医疗中心做检查。
words.en: A medical centre is a building or group of buildings where medical services are provided to the public.

words.tr: phrase. 健康中心；医疗中心（提供基本医疗服务的机构）
words.ex: He went to the health centre for a check-up.
words.ex_cn: 他去健康中心做检查。
words.en: A health centre is a building or a place where people can go for medical treatment or advice.

words.ex: He works at a small pharmacy near the park.
words.ex_cn: 他在公园附近的一家小药房工作。
words.en: A pharmacy is a shop or a department in a shop where medicines are prepared and sold.

words.ex: He bought medicine at the drugstore.
words.ex_cn: 他在药店买了药。
words.en: A drugstore is a shop where medicines and other small items are sold.

words.ex: He bought medicine at the chemist's.
words.ex_cn: 他在药房买了药。
words.en: A chemist's is a shop where medicines and other health-related products are sold, and where prescriptions can be filled.

words.ex: He went to the hospital because he felt sick.
words.ex_cn: 他因为感觉不舒服去了医院。
words.en: A hospital is a place where people who are ill or injured are treated and taken care of by doctors and nurses.

words.tr: phrase. 社区医院，为特定社区居民提供基本医疗服务的医疗机构
words.ex: The community hospital serves local families with basic medical care.
words.ex_cn: 社区医院为当地家庭提供基本医疗服务。
words.en: A community hospital is a hospital that primarily serves the health care needs of a specific community.

words.tr:
n. 练习；实践；惯常做法；
v. 从事；练习；
words.ex: Daily practice helps you improve your skills.
words.ex_cn: 每天的练习帮助你提高技能。
words.en: Practice is the act of rehearsing a behavior over and over, or engaging in an activity again and again, for the purpose of improving or mastering it, as in the phrase 'practice makes perfect'.

words.tr: n. 实践者；从业者；执业者；
words.ex: He is a medical practitioner who helps patients every day.
words.ex_cn: 他是一位每天帮助病人的医疗实践者。
words.en: A practitioner is someone who works in a particular profession, especially one that requires special training and skills.

words.ex: He visits his general practitioner for a check-up.
words.ex_cn: 他去看全科医生做体检。
words.en: A general practitioner is a doctor who does not specialize in one particular area of medicine, but who has a medical practice in which he or she treats all types of illness.

words.ex: The receptionist greeted the visitors with a smile.
words.ex_cn: 接待员微笑着迎接了访客。
words.en: A receptionist is a person whose job is to deal with people arriving at or telephoning a hotel, office building, doctor's surgery, etc.

words.ex: He is a consultant for a big company.
words.ex_cn: 他是这家大公司的顾问。
words.en: A consultant is a person who gives expert advice to a person or organization on a particular subject.

words.ex: The doctor helped the sick child.
words.ex_cn: 医生帮助了生病的孩子。
words.en: A doctor is someone who is qualified in medicine and treats people who are ill.

words.ex: He needs to see a doctor for his cough.
words.ex_cn: 他需要去看医生治咳嗽。
words.en: To visit a doctor for medical advice or treatment.

words.ex: When the child got sick, they sent for a doctor.
words.ex_cn: 当孩子生病时，他们请了医生来。
words.en: To ask someone to go and get a doctor to come to a place, especially in an emergency.

words.ex: He wants to register with a doctor near his home.
words.ex_cn: 他想在离家近的地方注册一位医生。
words.en: To officially sign up with a doctor or medical practice to receive healthcare services.

words.ex: The physician checked the patient's temperature.
words.ex_cn: 医生检查了病人的体温。
words.en: A physician is a medical doctor who is trained in the diagnosis and treatment of diseases and injuries.

words.ex: The surgeon fixed the broken bone.
words.ex_cn: 外科医生修复了断裂的骨头。
words.en: A surgeon is a medical doctor who performs operations.

words.ex: He visits the dentist every six months.
words.ex_cn: 他每六个月去看一次牙医。
words.en: A dentist is a person who is qualified to treat diseases and conditions that affect the teeth and gums, especially the repair and extraction of teeth and the insertion of artificial ones.

words.ex: The oculist checked his eyes last week.
words.ex_cn: 眼科医生上周检查了他的眼睛。
words.en: An oculist is a medical doctor who specializes in the diagnosis and treatment of eye disorders and diseases.

words.ex: He visited an eye doctor for a checkup.
words.ex_cn: 他去看眼科医生做检查。
words.en: A medical professional specializing in the diagnosis and treatment of eye disorders and diseases.

words.ex: The veterinarian helps sick animals.
words.ex_cn: 兽医帮助生病的动物。
words.en: A veterinarian is a person who is qualified to treat sick or injured animals.

words.tr:
n. 兽医；
v. 审查；
words.ex: The vet checked the dog's health.
words.ex_cn: 兽医检查了狗的健康状况。
words.en: A vet is a person who is qualified to treat sick or injured animals. As a verb, to vet means to examine something or someone carefully to make sure they are suitable for a particular purpose.

words.ex: The sweater shrinks in hot water.
words.ex_cn: 这件毛衣在热水中会收缩。
words.en: If something shrinks or you shrink it, it becomes smaller.

words.ex: He is a specialist in heart surgery.
words.ex_cn: 他是心脏手术方面的专家。
words.en: A specialist is a person who is highly skilled or knowledgeable in a particular field.

words.tr: phrase. 专业知识；专门知识
words.ex: He has specialist knowledge in computer science.
words.ex_cn: 他拥有计算机科学方面的专业知识。
words.en: Specialist knowledge refers to expert understanding or skill in a particular subject or field, often acquired through extensive study or experience.

words.ex: The nurse gave the patient medicine.
words.ex_cn: 护士给病人服了药。
words.en: A nurse is a person whose job is to care for people who are ill or injured, especially in a hospital.

words.ex: The children play at Nursery 796.
words.ex_cn: 孩子们在796号托儿所玩耍。
words.en: A nursery is a place where young children are cared for during the day while their parents are at work.

words.tr: adj. 精神病的；精神病学的；
words.ex: He works in a psychiatric hospital.
words.ex_cn: 他在一家精神病医院工作。
words.en: Psychiatric means relating to psychiatry or to mental illness.

words.tr: n. 精神病学家；精神科医生
words.ex: He visits a psychiatrist every week.
words.ex_cn: 他每周去看一次精神科医生。
words.en: A psychiatrist is a medical doctor who specializes in the diagnosis, treatment, and prevention of mental illnesses and emotional disorders.

words.tr:
n. 病人；
adj. 有耐心的；
words.ex: The doctor helped the patient feel better.
words.ex_cn: 医生帮助病人感觉好些了。
words.en: A patient person is able to wait for a long time or deal with a difficult situation without becoming angry or upset.

words.ex: I have an appointment with my doctor at 3 p.m.
words.ex_cn: 我下午三点有个医生的约会。
words.en: An appointment is a formal arrangement to meet or visit someone at a particular time, especially for a purpose connected with their work or official position.

words.ex: I will make an appointment with the doctor tomorrow.
words.ex_cn: 我明天要预约医生。
words.en: To arrange a meeting or consultation at a specific time.

words.tr: phrase. 预约系统；预约制度
words.ex: The hospital uses an appointment system to help patients.
words.ex_cn: 医院使用预约系统来帮助病人。
words.en: A method or process for scheduling and managing appointments, especially in a professional or medical setting.

words.ex: The ambulance arrived quickly to help the injured man.
words.ex_cn: 救护车迅速到达以帮助受伤的男人。
words.en: An ambulance is a vehicle equipped to transport the sick or injured, especially to a hospital.

words.ex: He had a check-up at the hospital last week.
words.ex_cn: 他上周在医院做了体检。
words.en: A check-up is a medical examination by your doctor to make sure that there is nothing wrong with your health.

words.tr: phrase. 体格检查；身体检查；体检
words.ex: The doctor performed a thorough physical examination.
words.ex_cn: 医生进行了一次全面的身体检查。
words.en: A physical examination is a routine test your primary care provider (PCP) performs to check your overall health. A PCP may be a doctor, a nurse practitioner, or a physician assistant. The exam is also known as a wellness check. You don't have to be sick to request an exam.

words.tr:
n. 收费；负责；指控；
v. 收费；充电；
words.ex: The hotel charge is $50 per night.
words.ex_cn: 酒店的收费是每晚50美元。
words.en: If you charge someone, you ask them to pay an amount of money for something that you have sold to them or done for them.

words.ex: The doctor treated his disease with medicine.
words.ex_cn: 医生用药物治疗了他的疾病。
words.en: A disease is an illness that affects people, animals, or plants, often caused by infection or a failure of health rather than by an accident.

words.ex: He was diagnosed with cancer last year.
words.ex_cn: 他去年被诊断出患有癌症。
words.en: Cancer is a serious disease caused by cells that are not normal and that can spread to other parts of the body.

words.tr:
n. 麻烦；问题；困难；
v. 费神；
words.ex: He got into trouble for breaking the rules.
words.ex_cn: 他因为违反规则而惹上了麻烦。
words.en: If you say that someone is in trouble, you mean that they are in a situation that is difficult to deal with and that may cause them problems.

words.ex: He has liver trouble from drinking too much.
words.ex_cn: 他因为喝酒太多而有肝脏问题。
words.en: Liver trouble refers to any disorder or disease affecting the liver, which can range from mild conditions like fatty liver to severe ones like cirrhosis.

words.tr: phrase. 背部问题；背痛；背部不适
words.ex: He has back trouble from sitting too long.
words.ex_cn: 他因为坐得太久而腰疼。
words.en: Pain or discomfort in the back, often due to strain, injury, or a chronic condition.

words.ex: He stayed home because he had the flu.
words.ex_cn: 他因为得了流感待在家里。
words.en: The flu is an infectious disease characterized by fever, aches and pains, and respiratory symptoms.

words.ex: He caught influenza last winter.
words.ex_cn: 他去年冬天得了流感。
words.en: Influenza is an infectious disease caused by the influenza virus, characterized by fever, sore throat, muscle pain, severe headache, coughing, and weakness.

words.ex: He has a high fever and stays in bed.
words.ex_cn: 他发烧了，躺在床上休息。
words.en: A fever is a condition in which the body's temperature is higher than usual, often as a response to infection.

words.ex: He have fever after running in the rain.
words.ex_cn: 他在雨中跑步后发烧了。
words.en: To have a higher than normal body temperature, often as a symptom of illness.

words.ex: He got yellow fever while traveling in Africa.
words.ex_cn: 他在非洲旅行时感染了黄热病。
words.en: Yellow fever is a serious viral disease that is transmitted by mosquitoes, primarily in tropical regions of Africa and South America. It is characterized by fever, chills, severe headache, back pain, general body aches, nausea, and vomiting. In severe cases, it can cause liver damage leading to jaundice (which gives the disease its name), bleeding, and even death.

words.ex: The temperature today is very high.
words.ex_cn: 今天的温度很高。
words.en: The degree or intensity of heat present in a substance or object, especially as expressed according to a comparative scale and shown by a thermometer or perceived by touch.

words.ex: He has temperature and needs to rest.
words.ex_cn: 他发烧了，需要休息。
words.en: To have a body temperature that is higher than normal, typically as a result of illness.

words.ex: The nurse takes her temperature every morning.
words.ex_cn: 护士每天早上给她量体温。
words.en: To measure someone's body temperature, usually to check for fever.

words.ex: He has an allergy to peanuts.
words.ex_cn: 他对花生过敏。
words.en: An allergy is a condition in which your immune system reacts abnormally to a foreign substance.

words.ex: He has a food allergy to peanuts.
words.ex_cn: 他对花生有食物过敏。
words.en: An adverse immune response to certain foods.

words.ex_cn: 他对花生过敏。
words.en: If you are allergic to something, you become ill or get a rash when you eat it, smell it, or touch it.

words.ex: He has insomnia and cannot sleep at night.
words.ex_cn: 他有失眠症，晚上睡不着。
words.en: If someone suffers from insomnia, they find it difficult to sleep.

words.ex: He has sleeplessness because of too much stress.
words.ex_cn: 他因为压力太大而失眠。
words.en: The condition of being unable to sleep.

words.ex: The wound caused a serious infection.
words.ex_cn: 伤口引起了严重的感染。
words.en: An infection is a disease caused by microorganisms such as bacteria, viruses, or parasites invading the body.

words.tr:
n. 毒药；毒物；
v. 毒害；
words.ex: The snake's poison can kill quickly.
words.ex_cn: 蛇的毒药能迅速致死。
words.en: A poison is a substance that causes harm or death if it is swallowed, absorbed, or breathed in. It can also refer to something that has a very harmful effect on something else.

words.ex: He got food poisoning from eating bad sushi.
words.ex_cn: 他吃了变质的寿司后食物中毒了。
words.en: Illness caused by consuming contaminated food, characterized by nausea, vomiting, diarrhea, and abdominal pain.

words.ex: He got pneumonia after a bad cold.
words.ex_cn: 他得了重感冒后患了肺炎。
words.en: Pneumonia is a serious disease which affects your lungs and makes it difficult for you to breathe.

words.ex: His eyesight is getting worse with age.
words.ex_cn: 他的视力随着年龄增长而变差。
words.en: Your eyesight is your ability to see.

words.tr: phrase. 视力差；近视或视力不良的状况
words.ex: He has bad eyesight and wears glasses.
words.ex_cn: 他视力不好，戴眼镜。
words.en: Poor vision or the inability to see well.

words.ex: He wears glasses because of poor eyesight.
words.ex_cn: 他因为视力不好而戴眼镜。
words.en: Impaired visual acuity or clarity, often requiring corrective lenses or indicating an underlying eye condition.

words.ex: He got malaria from a mosquito bite.
words.ex_cn: 他被蚊子叮咬后得了疟疾。
words.en: Malaria is a disease caused by a parasite that is transmitted to humans through the bites of infected mosquitoes.

words.ex: He has heart disease and must eat healthy food.
words.ex_cn: 他患有心脏病，必须吃健康的食物。
words.en: A condition that affects the heart and blood vessels, often leading to serious health issues.

words.ex: He had a heart attack last week.
words.ex_cn: 他上周心脏病发作。
words.en: A heart attack occurs when the flow of blood to the heart is blocked, usually by a blood clot.

words.ex: He got an injury while playing soccer.
words.ex_cn: 他在踢足球时受了伤。
words.en: An injury is damage to your body. It is a general term that refers to harm caused by accidents, falls, hits, weapons, etc.

words.tr: n. 伤口；创伤； v. “wind”的过去式和过去分词；
words.ex: He cleaned the wound with water.
words.ex_cn: 他用水清洗了伤口。
words.en: A wound is damage to part of your body, especially a cut or a hole in your flesh, which is caused by a gun, knife, or other weapon.

words.ex: He has a high fever as a symptom of the flu.
words.ex_cn: 他发烧是流感的症状。
words.en: A symptom is a physical or mental feature which is regarded as indicating a condition of disease, particularly such a feature that is apparent to the patient.

words.tr: n. 头痛；令人头痛的人（或事物）；
words.ex: He got a headache after working too long.
words.ex_cn: 他工作太长时间后得了头痛。
words.en: A headache is a pain in your head. If you say that something is a headache, you mean that it causes you difficulty or worry.

words.ex: He has a stomach-ache after eating too much candy.
words.ex_cn: 他吃了太多糖果后肚子疼。
words.en: A pain in the stomach, typically caused by indigestion or illness.

words.ex: He has a toothache and cannot eat.
words.ex_cn: 他牙疼，不能吃东西。
words.en: A toothache is a pain in or around a tooth.

words.tr:
n. 咳嗽；
v. 咳嗽；
words.ex: He had a bad cough last night.
words.ex_cn: 他昨晚咳得很厉害。
words.en: A cough is a sudden, forceful expulsion of air from the lungs, often caused by irritation in the airway.

words.ex: My throat is sore after singing.
words.ex_cn: 我唱歌后喉咙疼。
words.en: If part of your body is sore, it causes you pain and discomfort.

words.ex: He has a sore throat from singing too much.
words.ex_cn: 他因为唱太多歌而喉咙痛。
words.en: If you have a sore throat, your throat hurts and it is difficult for you to swallow.

words.tr: adj. 头晕目眩的；头昏眼花的；
words.ex: He felt dizzy after spinning around quickly.
words.ex_cn: 他快速转圈后感到头晕目眩。
words.en: If you feel dizzy, you feel that you are losing your balance and are about to fall.

words.ex: He gave the rope a twist to tie it tight.
words.ex_cn: 他把绳子拧了一下以便系紧。
words.en: To twist something means to turn it in a different direction or to change its shape by turning it.

words.ex: He has a big nose.
words.ex_cn: 他有一个大鼻子。
words.en: The part of the face or head that contains the nostrils and organs of smell and through which a person or animal breathes.

words.ex: He has a stuffed nose from the cold.
words.ex_cn: 他因为感冒而鼻塞。
words.en: A stuffed nose refers to the condition where the nasal passages are blocked, often due to inflammation of the nasal tissues, making it difficult to breathe through the nose.

words.ex: He has a running nose because of the cold.
words.ex_cn: 他因为感冒而流鼻涕。
words.en: A condition where liquid drips from the nose.

words.tr: adj. 昏昏欲睡的；困倦的；催眠的
words.ex: He felt drowsy after lunch.
words.ex_cn: 他午饭后感到昏昏欲睡。
words.en: If you feel drowsy, you feel sleepy and cannot think clearly.

words.ex: He felt fatigued after running for an hour.
words.ex_cn: 他跑了一小时后感到疲惫。
words.en: Feeling very tired, especially as a result of excessive exertion or lack of sleep.

words.tr: adj. 筋疲力尽的；耗尽的； v. 耗尽；用完；“exhaust”的过去式和过去分词；
words.ex: He was exhausted after running five kilometers.
words.ex_cn: 他跑完五公里后筋疲力尽。
words.en: If you are exhausted, you are very tired and have no energy left.

words.ex: The epidemic spread quickly across the country.
words.ex_cn: 这种流行病迅速蔓延到全国。
words.en: An epidemic is a large number of cases of an infectious disease occurring at the same time.

words.tr: phrase. 流行病；传染病大规模爆发的疾病
words.ex: The government is taking measures to control the epidemic disease.
words.ex_cn: 政府正在采取措施控制这种流行病。
words.en: An epidemic disease is a disease that spreads rapidly among many people in a community at the same time.

words.ex: The doctor checked his pulse with his fingers.
words.ex_cn: 医生用手指检查了他的脉搏。
words.en: A pulse is the regular beating of the heart, especially when it is felt at the wrist or neck. It can also refer to a single vibration or short burst of sound, electric current, light, etc.

words.ex: The doctor feels his patient's pulse every morning.
words.ex_cn: 医生每天早上都摸病人的脉搏。
words.en: To feel someone's pulse is to check their heart rate by pressing on their wrist, or to try to find out someone's opinions or feelings about something.

words.tr:
n. 压力；压强；
v. 对…施加压力；
words.ex: He feels pressure from his parents to get good grades.
words.ex_cn: 他感受到来自父母要取得好成绩的压力。
words.en: Pressure is the force that you produce when you press hard on something, or the force that is produced by a particular amount of gas or liquid in a confined space.

words.tr: phrase. 高血压；动脉血压持续升高的病症
words.ex: He has high blood pressure and must eat less salt.
words.ex_cn: 他有高血压，必须少吃盐。
words.en: High blood pressure is a condition in which the force of the blood against the artery walls is too high.

words.ex: The doctor wrote a prescription for medicine.
words.ex_cn: 医生开了一张药方。
words.en: A prescription is a written order from a physician for the preparation and administration of a drug or device for a patient.

words.ex: The doctor gave a prescription for medicine.
words.ex_cn: 医生开了药方。
words.en: To issue a written order for medication or treatment from a doctor.

words.tr: n. 药物；药物治疗；药物处理；
words.ex: He took his medication every morning.
words.ex_cn: 他每天早上吃药。
words.en: Medication refers to a substance used for medical treatment, especially a medicine or drug.

words.ex: The doctor suggested a natural remedy for the cold.
words.ex_cn: 医生建议了一种治疗感冒的天然疗法。
words.en: A remedy is a cure or a way of making something better.

words.ex: He is receiving therapy for his back pain.
words.ex_cn: 他正在接受治疗以缓解背痛。
words.en: Therapy is the treatment of someone with mental or physical illness without the use of drugs or operations.

words.ex: The doctor gave him proper treatment for the infection.
words.ex_cn: 医生给他提供了针对感染的适当治疗。
words.en: The act or manner of treating someone or something, especially in a medical context.

words.tr: phrase. 放松疗法；通过呼吸、冥想、渐进性肌肉放松等手段减轻压力与焦虑的心理或生理治疗方法
words.ex: He uses relaxation therapy to reduce stress.
words.ex_cn: 他使用放松疗法来减轻压力。
words.en: Relaxation therapy refers to a variety of techniques designed to teach a person to be able to relax voluntarily. It is often used to reduce stress, anxiety, and tension.

words.ex: The doctor can diagnose the illness quickly.
words.ex_cn: 医生能很快诊断出这种病。
words.en: If someone or something is diagnosed as having a particular illness or problem, their illness or problem is identified. If an illness or problem is diagnosed, it is identified.

words.ex: Wear a helmet as a precaution when riding a bike.
words.ex_cn: 骑自行车时戴头盔作为一种预防措施。
words.en: A precaution is an action that is intended to prevent something dangerous or unpleasant from happening.

words.tr:
n. 锻炼；行使；练习；
v. 运用；使用；锻炼；
words.ex: He does exercise every morning to stay healthy.
words.ex_cn: 他每天早上锻炼以保持健康。
words.en: Physical activity that you do to make your body strong and healthy.

words.ex: The doctor gave him an injection for the pain.
words.ex_cn: 医生给他打了一针来缓解疼痛。
words.en: An injection is the act of putting a liquid, especially a drug, into a person's body using a needle and a syringe.

words.ex: The operation of the machine is very smooth.
words.ex_cn: 这台机器的运行非常顺畅。
words.en: An operation is a planned activity involving many people performing various tasks.

words.ex: He wants to study medicine at university.
words.ex_cn: 他想在大学学习医学。
words.en: Medicine is the science or practice of the diagnosis, treatment, and prevention of disease.

words.ex: He took a pill for his headache.
words.ex_cn: 他吃了一粒药丸来缓解头痛。
words.en: A pill is a small solid mass of medicine that you swallow whole.

words.tr: n. 平板电脑；（刻有文字的）匾；
words.ex: He uses a tablet to read books.
words.ex_cn: 他用平板电脑读书。
words.en: A tablet is a small, flat computer that is controlled by touching the screen. It can also refer to a small, solid piece of medicine that you swallow.

words.ex: He poured syrup on his pancakes.
words.ex_cn: 他把糖浆倒在煎饼上。
words.en: A thick, sweet liquid made by dissolving sugar in boiling water, often used as a topping for desserts or as a sweetener in drinks.

words.ex: The doctor gave me an antibiotic for my infection.
words.ex_cn: 医生给我开了抗菌素治疗感染。
words.en: A substance that can kill or inhibit the growth of bacteria and other microorganisms.

words.tr: n. 阿司匹林（镇痛解热消炎药）
words.ex: He took aspirin for his headache.
words.ex_cn: 他吃了阿司匹林来缓解头痛。
words.en: Aspirin is a common drug that is used to reduce pain and inflammation.

words.ex: Eating fruits gives you vitamin C.
words.ex_cn: 吃水果可以给你维生素C。
words.en: A vitamin is one of a group of organic substances which are essential in small quantities to the nutrition of most animals and some plants, and which are present in natural foodstuffs or sometimes produced within the body.

words.tr:
n. 绷带
v. 用绷带包扎
words.ex: He put a bandage on his cut finger.
words.ex_cn: 他在他割伤的手指上贴了绷带。
words.en: A bandage is a piece of material used to cover a wound or to support an injured part of the body.

words.tr:
v. 粘附；（随意）放置；忍受；
n. 棍枝；条状物；球棍；
words.ex: The glue makes the paper stick to the table.
words.ex_cn: 胶水使纸粘在桌子上。
words.en: A stick is a thin branch which has fallen off a tree. If you stick something somewhere, you put it there in a rather casual way.

words.ex: He took a capsule for his headache.
words.ex_cn: 他吃了一粒胶囊来缓解头痛。
words.en: A capsule is a small container or case, especially one that is sealed and contains a dose of medicine, or a spacecraft's compartment for astronauts.

words.ex: He took a painkiller for his headache.
words.ex_cn: 他吃了一片止痛药来缓解头痛。
words.en: A painkiller is a drug that reduces or removes physical pain.

words.tr:
v. 落下；掉下；
n. 滴；下落；
words.ex: The apple dropped from the tree.
words.ex_cn: 苹果从树上落了下来。
words.en: If you drop something, you accidentally let it fall.

words.ex: He uses eyedrops when his eyes feel dry.
words.ex_cn: 当他的眼睛感到干涩时，他会使用眼药水。
words.en: A liquid medicine that is dropped into the eyes to treat or prevent eye conditions.

words.ex: He got a vaccine last week.
words.ex_cn: 他上周打了疫苗。
words.en: A vaccine is a substance containing a virus or bacterium in a form that is not harmful, given to a person or animal to prevent them from getting the disease that the virus or bacterium causes.

words.tr: phrase. 疫苗注射；接种疫苗
words.ex: The nurse gave an injection of vaccine to the child.
words.ex_cn: 护士给小孩注射了疫苗。
words.en: The administration of a vaccine into the body, typically via a needle.

words.tr:
n. 面试；访谈；
v. 面试；接见；
words.ex: He has an interview tomorrow for a new job.
words.ex_cn: 他明天有一场新工作的面试。
words.en: An interview is a formal meeting at which someone is asked questions in order to find out if they are suitable for a job or a course of study.

words.ex: The interviewer asked him about his work experience.
words.ex_cn: 采访者问他关于他的工作经验。
words.en: An interviewer is a person who asks someone questions at an interview.

words.tr: n. 被面试者；被采访者；
words.ex: The interviewee answered all the questions calmly.
words.ex_cn: 被面试者冷静地回答了所有问题。
words.en: A person who is interviewed.

words.ex: He is a candidate for the mayor position.
words.ex_cn: 他是市长职位的候选人。
words.en: A candidate is someone who is being considered for a position, for example someone who is running in an election or applying for a job.

words.ex: The company plans to recruit new staff next month.
words.ex_cn: 这家公司计划下个月招聘新员工。
words.en: To recruit means to enlist someone in the armed forces or to persuade someone to join a company, organization, or group.

words.ex: The company will hire a new manager next week.
words.ex_cn: 公司下周将雇用一位新经理。
words.en: If you hire someone, you employ them or pay them to do a particular job for you.

words.tr:
n. 火；
v. 射击；开火；
words.ex: The fire burned brightly in the fireplace.
words.ex_cn: 火在壁炉里熊熊燃烧。
words.en: Fire is the heat and light that comes out when something burns. It can also refer to the act of shooting a weapon or the dismissal of an employee from a job.

words.tr:
n. 袋子；
v. 劫掠；
words.ex: He carried the apples in a burlap sack.
words.ex_cn: 他把苹果装在一个麻布袋里。
words.en: A sack is a large bag made of rough woven material, used for storing or carrying goods. It can also refer to the act of dismissing someone from employment or the act of looting a place.

words.ex: He was sacked for being late to work three times in a week.
words.ex_cn: v. 他因为一周内迟到三次而被解雇。
words.en: To be dismissed from employment, typically for reasons of incompetence or misconduct.

words.ex: He got the sack because he was always late.
words.ex_cn: 他因为总是迟到而被解雇了。
words.en: If you get the sack, you are dismissed from your job.

words.ex: The company will employ five new workers next month.
words.ex_cn: 这家公司下个月将雇佣五名新员工。
words.en: If a person or company employs you, they pay you to work for them.

words.ex: He found employment after graduating from university.
words.ex_cn: 他大学毕业后找到了工作。
words.en: the condition of having paid work

words.ex: Many people face unemployment during the economic crisis.
words.ex_cn: 在经济危机期间，许多人面临失业。
words.en: Unemployment refers to the state of being without a job, especially when one is actively seeking employment.

words.ex: The unemployment rate went up last month.
words.ex_cn: 上个月失业率上升了。
words.en: The unemployment rate is the percentage of the labor force that is jobless and actively seeking employment.

words.ex: He chose self-employment after losing his job.
words.ex_cn: 他在失业后选择了自主就业。
words.en: Self-employment refers to the state of working for oneself as a freelance or the owner of a business rather than for an employer.

words.ex: He will retire next year.
words.ex_cn: 他明年将退休。
words.en: If you retire, you stop working, usually because you have reached a certain age or because you are ill.

words.ex: He plans to start his retirement next year.
words.ex_cn: 他计划明年退休。
words.en: Retirement is the period of one's life after leaving one's job and ceasing to work.

words.ex: He got a new job last week.
words.ex_cn: 他上周找到了一份新工作。
words.en: A job is the work that someone does regularly in order to earn money.

words.ex: He is a job hunter looking for work.
words.ex_cn: 他是一名求职者，正在找工作。
words.en: A person who is seeking employment.

words.tr: phrase. 求职者；找工作的人
words.ex: He is a job seeker looking for work.
words.ex_cn: 他是一名正在找工作的人。
words.en: A job seeker is someone who is trying to find employment.

words.tr: phrase. 就业前景；工作前景；职业前途
words.ex: He wants to improve his job prospect by learning new skills.
words.ex_cn: 他想通过学习新技能来改善就业前景。
words.en: The possibility or likelihood of future success in a job or career.

words.ex: The occupation of the city by foreign troops lasted for years.
words.ex_cn: 外国军队对这座城市的占领持续了多年。
words.en: An occupation is a job or profession, or a way of spending your time.

words.tr: n. 劳动力；工人总数；职工总数；
words.ex: The factory needs a larger workforce to meet demand.
words.ex_cn: 工厂需要更多的劳动力来满足需求。
words.en: The workforce is the total number of people who are employed by a particular company or who are available to work in a particular country or area.

words.tr:
n. 压力；压强；
v. 对…施加压力；
words.ex: He feels pressure from his parents to get good grades.
words.ex_cn: 他感受到来自父母要取得好成绩的压力。
words.en: Pressure is the force that you produce when you press hard on something, or the force that is produced by a particular amount of gas or liquid in a confined space.

words.tr:
n. 压力；强调；
v. 着重；强调；
words.ex: He feels stress from too much work.
words.ex_cn: 他因为工作太多而感到压力。
words.en: Stress is a state of mental or emotional strain or tension resulting from adverse or demanding circumstances.

words.tr:
n. 压力；（动植物的）品种；
v. 竭力；
words.ex: The job gave him a lot of strain.
words.ex_cn: 这份工作给他带来了很大的压力。
words.en: To strain means to make a great effort to do something, to pull or stretch something tightly, or to injure a muscle by stretching it too much.

words.ex: He gets a salary of 3000 dollars each month.
words.ex_cn: 他每个月赚3000美元的工资。
words.en: A salary is the money that someone is paid each month by their employer, especially when they are in a profession such as teaching, law, or medicine.

words.ex: He receives his wage every Friday.
words.ex_cn: 他每周五领工资。
words.en: A wage is the money that someone is paid each week by their employer, especially for manual or unskilled work. To wage means to carry on (a war or campaign).

words.ex: He made the payment online.
words.ex_cn: 他在线支付了。
words.en: A payment is an amount of money that is paid to someone, or the act of paying this money.

words.tr: n. 委员会；委托；佣金；任务；[军] 职务；[律] 委任状；v. 委托；任命；给...以任务
words.ex: He got a commission for selling the car.
words.ex_cn: 他因为卖了这辆车而获得了佣金。
words.en: A misspelling of 'commission', meaning an order for work or a fee for services.

words.tr: adj. 工资高的（工作）；收入高的（人）
words.ex: He is a well-paid engineer.
words.ex_cn: 他是一名高薪的工程师。
words.en: A well-paid job or position is one for which you are paid a lot of money.

words.ex: The bonus is an incentive to work harder.
words.ex_cn: 奖金是努力工作的动机。
words.en: Something that encourages a person to do something or to work harder.

words.tr:
n. 奖励；报酬；
v. 奖励；回报；
words.ex: He got a reward for winning the contest.
words.ex_cn: 他因赢得比赛而得到了奖励。
words.en: Something given or received in return for a deed or service rendered.

words.tr: adj. 有益的；值得的； v. “reward”的现在分词；
words.ex: Volunteering is a rewarding experience.
words.ex_cn: 志愿服务是一种有益的经历。
words.en: Providing satisfaction or gratification; beneficial.

words.ex: I have an appointment with my doctor at 3 p.m.
words.ex_cn: 我下午三点有个医生的约会。
words.en: An appointment is a formal arrangement to meet or visit someone at a particular time, especially for a purpose connected with their work or official position.

words.ex: They will nominate her for the award.
words.ex_cn: 他们将提名她获得这个奖项。
words.en: If someone is nominated for a job or position, their name is formally suggested as a candidate for it.

words.tr: v. 促进；推动；宣传；推销；
words.ex: Exercise can promote good health.
words.ex_cn: 锻炼可以促进健康。
words.en: To promote means to help something to happen, develop, or increase, or to raise someone to a higher position or rank.

words.ex: He got promoted after working hard for two years.
words.ex_cn: 他努力工作两年后得到了晋升。
words.en: To be raised to a higher rank or position, especially at work.

words.ex: The new policy is for the promotion of clean energy.
words.ex_cn: 这项新政策是为了促进清洁能源。
words.en: A promotion is a move to a more important job or rank in a company or organization.

words.ex: He worked hard to accomplish his goal.
words.ex_cn: 他努力工作以实现自己的目标。
words.en: To accomplish something means to succeed in doing it, especially after a lot of effort.

words.ex: He felt proud of his academic achievement.
words.ex_cn: 他为自己的学业成就感到自豪。
words.en: An achievement is something which someone has succeeded in doing, especially after a lot of effort.

words.tr:
n. 经验；阅历；
v. 经历；体验；
words.ex: He has a lot of experience in teaching English.
words.ex_cn: 他有丰富的英语教学经验。
words.en: Experience is knowledge or skill in a particular job or activity that you have gained because you have done that job or activity for a long time.

words.tr: phrase. 工作经验；职业经历
words.ex: He has work experience in a restaurant.
words.ex_cn: 他在餐厅有工作经验。
words.en: Work experience refers to the knowledge and skills that someone has gained through working in a particular job or field.

words.tr:
n. 形式；表格；形状；
v. 组成；建立；
words.ex: The form of the poem is very simple.
words.ex_cn: 这首诗的形式非常简单。
words.en: A form is a particular way in which a thing exists or appears, or a document with spaces in which to write information.

words.ex: He filled out the application form yesterday.
words.ex_cn: 他昨天填了申请表。
words.en: A document used to apply for something, such as a job or membership, by providing personal information and details.

words.tr: abbr. 简历；履历；“curriculum vitae”的缩写
words.ex: He sent his cv to the company.
words.ex_cn: 他把简历发给了公司。
words.en: A document that summarizes a person's education, work experience, and other qualifications for a job.

words.ex: He sent his curriculum vitae to the company.
words.ex_cn: 他把简历发给了公司。
words.en: A curriculum vitae is a written account of your education and the jobs you have done, which you send when you are applying for a job.

words.ex: After a short break, he resumed his work.
words.ex_cn: 短暂休息后，他继续工作。
words.en: If you resume an activity or if it resumes, it begins again or continues after an interruption.

words.ex: A is the first letter in the English alphabet.
words.ex_cn: A 是英语字母表中的第一个字母。
words.en: A letter is a written message that can be handwritten or printed on paper. It is usually sent in an envelope by post or messenger.

words.ex: He asked his teacher for a recommendation letter.
words.ex_cn: 他请老师写一封推荐信。
words.en: A letter written by someone who knows you well, usually a teacher or employer, that describes your abilities and qualities and is sent to a potential employer, university, etc.

words.tr: phrase. 求职信；附函（随简历或文件一同寄出的说明信）
words.ex: He wrote a cover letter for his job application.
words.ex_cn: 他为他的工作申请写了一封求职信。
words.en: A cover letter is a document sent with your resume to provide additional information on your skills and experience. The letter typically provides detailed information on why you are qualified for the job you are applying for.

words.tr: phrase. 申请信；求职信（申请人向招聘单位提交的表达求职意愿的信件）
words.ex: He wrote an applicant letter for the job.
words.ex_cn: 他为这份工作写了一封求职信。
words.en: A written document submitted by a job seeker to an employer, detailing their qualifications and interest in a position.

words.tr: n. 参考；提及；介绍信；引用；
words.ex: Please use this book for reference.
words.ex_cn: 请使用这本书作为参考。
words.en: A reference is a mention of something or someone, or a letter or statement about someone's character or abilities.

words.ex: He asked his teacher for a letter of reference.
words.ex_cn: 他请老师写一封推荐信。
words.en: A letter of reference is a letter in which someone who knows you well writes about your character and abilities, usually for the purpose of helping you get a job or a place at a college or university.

words.ex: He is on probation for one year.
words.ex_cn: 他被判缓刑一年。
words.en: Probation is a period of time during which someone who has committed a crime has to behave well and not commit any more crimes in order to avoid being sent to prison.

words.tr:
v. 做实习生；扣留
n. 实习生
words.ex: He is interning at a hospital this summer.
words.ex_cn: 他今年夏天在医院做实习生。
words.en: An intern is someone who works in a temporary position with an emphasis on on-the-job training rather than merely employment, often to gain experience in a particular field.

words.ex: He did an internship at a hospital last summer.
words.ex_cn: 去年夏天，他在一家医院实习。
words.en: An internship is a period of work experience offered by an organization for a limited period of time. It is typically undertaken by students and graduates looking to gain relevant skills and experience in a particular field.

words.tr:
n. 转移；移位；转变；轮班；
v. 变换位置；转移；换（挡）；轮班；
words.ex: The shift of power to the new government was sudden.
words.ex_cn: 权力向新政府的转移是突然的。
words.en: If you shift something or if it shifts, it moves or changes its position slightly. If someone's opinion, attitude, or behaviour shifts, it changes slightly, especially in response to a particular situation or event.

words.tr: phrase. 白班；日班（指在白天工作的轮班）
words.ex: He works the day shift at the hospital.
words.ex_cn: 他在医院上白班。
words.en: A day shift refers to a period of time during the day, typically from early morning to late afternoon, when a person is scheduled to work.

words.ex: He works the night shift at the hospital.
words.ex_cn: 他在医院上夜班。
words.en: A night shift is a period of work that occurs during the night, typically from late evening to early morning, in various industries and services.

words.tr: phrase. 替代某人值勤；替某人顶班
words.ex: I will cover the shift for Sarah tonight.
words.ex_cn: 今晚我会替萨拉值勤。

words.ex: He took a day-off to rest at home.
words.ex_cn: 他请了一天假在家休息。
words.en: A day-off refers to a day when one does not have to work or attend school, typically used for rest or leisure activities.

words.ex: He works in the sales department.
words.ex_cn: 他在销售部工作。
words.en: A department is one of the sections in an organization such as a government, business, or university.

words.ex: The sales department sends out invoices every week.
words.ex_cn: 销售部门每周发送发票。
words.en: The division of a business responsible for selling products or services.

words.ex: He works in the personnel department.
words.ex_cn: 他在人事部门工作。
words.en: The department within a company that deals with the hiring, administration, and training of staff.

words.tr: phrase. 财务部门；负责公司或组织财务管理、会计和资金运作的部门
words.ex: He works in the finance department.
words.ex_cn: 他在财务部门工作。
words.en: The finance department is the division of a business that is responsible for obtaining and managing funds, including budgeting, accounting, and financial reporting.

words.ex: The marketing department sent out new ads last week.
words.ex_cn: 市场部上周发布了新广告。
words.en: The section of a company responsible for promoting and selling products.

words.tr: phrase. 质量控制部门；品管部
words.ex: The quality control department checks every product.
words.ex_cn: 质量控制部门检查每一件产品。
words.en: The department within a company responsible for ensuring products meet specific standards of quality.

words.ex: There is a vacancy in the sales department.
words.ex_cn: 销售部门有一个空缺职位。
words.en: A vacancy is a position or job that is available for someone to fill.

words.tr: n. 位置；职位；地位；姿势；
words.ex: The book is on the table in a good position.
words.ex_cn: 书放在桌子上的一个好位置。
words.en: A position refers to the place or type of role someone has in a situation, organization, or society, or the way in which someone or something is placed or arranged.

words.tr: n. 主席；主持人；董事长；
words.ex: The chairman called the meeting to order.
words.ex_cn: 主席宣布会议开始。
words.en: A chairman is a man who is in charge of a meeting, committee, or organization.

words.ex: The president signed the new contract.
words.ex_cn: 总裁签署了新合同。
words.en: The president is the elected head of a republic or the head of a company or organization.

words.ex: The manager approved the new project.
words.ex_cn: 经理批准了新项目。
words.en: A manager is a person who is responsible for running part of or the whole of a business organization.

words.tr:
n. 代表；典型事物；
adj. 典型的；有代表性的；代议制的；
words.ex: He is the representative of our class.
words.ex_cn: 他是我们班的代表。
words.en: A representative is a person who has been chosen to act or make decisions on behalf of another person or a group of people.

words.ex: The supervisor checked the workers' progress.
words.ex_cn: 主管检查了工人们的进展。
words.en: A supervisor is a person who oversees and directs the work of others.

words.ex: The staff at the hotel are very friendly.
words.ex_cn: 酒店的职员非常友好。
words.en: The people who work for a particular organization or company, or a group of officers assisting a commanding officer.

words.ex: The waiter brought us water and menus.
words.ex_cn: 服务员给我们端来了水和菜单。
words.en: A waiter is a man who works in a restaurant, serving people with food and drink.

words.ex: The waitress brought us water and menus.
words.ex_cn: 女服务员给我们端来了水和菜单。
words.en: A waitress is a woman who works in a restaurant, serving food and drink to customers.

words.ex: The clerk at the store helped me find the book.
words.ex_cn: 商店里的职员帮我找到了那本书。
words.en: A clerk is a person whose job is to keep records or accounts in an office, shop, or bank.

words.tr: phrase. 银行职员；银行办事员
words.ex: He works as a bank clerk in the city.
words.ex_cn: 他在城里当银行职员。
words.en: A bank clerk is a person employed by a bank to deal with customers' transactions and provide information about the bank's services.

words.ex: My colleague helped me with the report.
words.ex_cn: 我的同事帮我完成了报告。
words.en: A colleague is someone you work with, especially in a professional job.

words.tr: adj. 蓝领阶级的；体力劳动的
words.ex: He is a blue-collar worker who fixes cars.
words.ex_cn: 他是一名修车的蓝领工人。
words.en: Blue-collar refers to work or workers who do manual labor, typically in industry, as opposed to white-collar workers who perform professional, managerial, or administrative work.

words.tr: adj. 白领阶层的；脑力劳动的
words.ex: He works as a white-collar worker in an office.
words.ex_cn: 他在办公室做白领工作。
words.en: Relating to the work done or the people who work in an office or other professional environment.

words.tr:
adj. 一致的；统一的；
n. 制服；
words.ex: The students wear a uniform shirt to school.
words.ex_cn: 学生们穿一致的衬衫去学校。
words.en: A uniform is a special set of clothes which some people, for example soldiers or the police, wear to work in and which some children wear at school. It is also used to describe something that is the same in all parts and does not vary.

words.tr:
v. 适合；相配；
n. 套装；西装；诉讼；
words.ex: This color suits her well.
words.ex_cn: 这个颜色很适合她。
words.en: A suit is a set of clothes made from the same fabric, usually consisting of a jacket and trousers or a skirt. As a verb, to suit means to be appropriate or acceptable for someone or something.

words.ex: He works as an accountant in a small company.
words.ex_cn: 他在一家小公司当会计师。
words.en: An accountant is a person whose job is to keep, inspect, and analyze financial accounts.

words.ex: The teacher has an assistant to help with grading.
words.ex_cn: 老师有一个助理帮忙批改作业。
words.en: An assistant is a person who helps in particular work or who is under the authority of another person.

words.tr: phrase. 图书馆助理；图书管理员助理
words.ex: He works as a library assistant at the school.
words.ex_cn: 他在学校担任图书管理员助理。
words.en: A library assistant is a person who helps in the running of a library, performing tasks such as organizing books, helping library users, and managing library resources.

words.ex: He works as an office assistant in a small company.
words.ex_cn: 他在一家小公司担任办公室助理。
words.en: An office assistant is a person who helps to manage the day-to-day operations of an office, performing tasks such as answering phones, scheduling appointments, and organizing files.

words.tr: n. 清洁工人；清洁工具； adj. 更洁净的；更干净的；“clean”的比较级；
words.ex: The cleaner sweeps the floor every morning.
words.ex_cn: 清洁工人每天早上扫地。
words.en: A cleaner is a person whose job is to clean a place or a substance used for cleaning.

words.ex: She is a fast typist.
words.ex_cn: 她是一位打字很快的打字员。
words.en: A typist is someone who types, especially as their job.

words.ex: We ate dinner at a small restaurant.
words.ex_cn: 我们在一家小餐厅吃了晚饭。
words.en: A restaurant is a place where you can eat a meal and pay for it. In restaurants, your food is usually served to you at your table by a waiter or waitress.

words.tr: phrase. 中餐馆；提供中式菜肴的餐厅
words.ex: We ate dinner at a chinese restaurant.
words.ex_cn: 我们在一家中餐馆吃了晚饭。
words.en: A Chinese restaurant is a restaurant that serves Chinese cuisine.

words.tr: phrase. 印度餐厅；供应印度菜肴的餐馆
words.ex: We had a delicious meal at the Indian restaurant.
words.ex_cn: 我们在那家印度餐厅享用了一顿美味的餐点。
words.en: An Indian restaurant is a type of restaurant that specializes in Indian cuisine, offering a variety of dishes that are typical of Indian culinary traditions.

words.ex: We ate tacos at a small mexico restaurant.
words.ex_cn: 我们在一家小型墨西哥餐厅吃了玉米饼。
words.en: A restaurant that specializes in Mexican cuisine, offering dishes such as tacos, enchiladas, and burritos.

words.ex: We had tea in the tea room.
words.ex_cn: 我们在茶室喝了茶。
words.en: A room or establishment where tea is served, often with light meals or snacks.

words.ex: I had coffee at a small caf near the park.
words.ex_cn: 我在公园附近的一家小咖啡馆喝了咖啡。
words.en: A small restaurant or coffee shop that serves light meals and drinks.

words.tr: n. 自助餐厅；自助食堂；
words.ex: We ate lunch in the school cafeteria.
words.ex_cn: 我们在学校自助餐厅吃午饭。
words.en: A cafeteria is a type of food service location within an institution in which there is little or no waiting staff table service, whether a restaurant or within an institution such as a large office building or school; a school dining location is also referred to as a dining hall or canteen (in British English).

words.ex: We had dinner at a buffet with many dishes to choose from.
words.ex_cn: 我们在自助餐吃了晚饭，有很多菜可以选。
words.en: A buffet is a meal consisting of several dishes from which guests serve themselves. As a verb, to buffet means to strike repeatedly and violently.

words.tr: n. 条状物；酒吧；栅栏；棒；
words.ex: He ate a chocolate bar after dinner.
words.ex_cn: 他晚饭后吃了一条巧克力。
words.en: A bar is a place where alcoholic drinks are served, or a long, narrow piece of metal or wood used for a particular purpose.

words.ex: He drinks coffee at the coffee bar every morning.
words.ex_cn: 他每天早上在咖啡吧喝咖啡。
words.en: A coffee bar is an establishment that primarily serves coffee and other hot beverages, often with light snacks and pastries.

words.ex: He picked his dinner from the salad bar.
words.ex_cn: 他从沙拉吧挑选了他的晚餐。
words.en: A salad bar is a buffet-style table or counter at a restaurant or food service facility where customers can assemble their own salad plates from a variety of ingredients.

words.tr: n. 外带食物；外卖；要点；诀窍
words.ex: I bought a take-away pizza for dinner.
words.ex_cn: 我买了一份外带披萨当晚餐。
words.en: A meal prepared at a restaurant to be eaten elsewhere.

words.ex: He ordered a take-away pizza for dinner.
words.ex_cn: 他订了一份外带披萨当晚餐。
words.en: Pizza that is prepared to be taken away and eaten elsewhere.

words.ex: We eat at a take-away restaurant every Friday.
words.ex_cn: 我们每周五在快餐店吃饭。
words.en: A take-away restaurant is a place where you can buy food to eat somewhere else, rather than eating it in the restaurant.

words.tr: 短语动词. 在家吃饭；不在外面餐馆用餐
words.ex: We eat in on weekends.
words.ex_cn: 我们在周末在家吃饭。
words.en: To eat a meal at home rather than in a restaurant.

words.tr: 短语动词。离开；出发；将要发生；（食物等）可外带
words.ex: He went to go to school early.
words.ex_cn: 他出发去学校了。
words.en: To travel or move from one place to another.

words.w: a cup of coffee to go
words.uk: ə kʌp əv ˈkɒfi tu ɡəʊ
words.us: ə kʌp əv ˈkɔːfi tu ɡoʊ
words.ex: She ordered a cup of coffee to go before heading to the office.
words.ex_cn: 她在去办公室之前点了一杯外带的咖啡。
words.en: A cup of coffee purchased to be taken away and consumed elsewhere.

words.tr:
adj. 免下车即可得到服务的
n. 免下车餐馆；免下车电影院；免下车商业场所
words.ex: We ate burgers at a drive-in last night.
words.ex_cn: 我们昨晚在汽车餐厅吃了汉堡。
words.en: A drive-in is a place such as a restaurant or cinema where you can be served or watch a film without leaving your car.

words.ex: She put the food on a clean plate.
words.ex_cn: 她把食物放在一个干净的盘子里。
words.en: A flat dish, typically circular and made of china, from which food is eaten or served.

words.ex: He placed the cups on a tray.
words.ex_cn: 他把杯子放在一个托盘上。
words.en: A tray is a flat container, usually made of wood, plastic, or metal, with raised edges, used for carrying things such as food or drinks.

words.tr:
n. 叉子；分岔；分支
v. 分岔；用叉子叉
words.ex: He picked up a fork to eat his pasta.
words.ex_cn: 他拿起叉子吃意大利面。
words.en: A fork is a tool used for eating or serving food, consisting of a handle with several narrow tines on one end. It can also refer to a division into two or more branches or directions.

words.ex: He cut the bread with a knife.
words.ex_cn: 他用刀切面包。
words.en: A knife is a tool for cutting or a weapon, consisting of a flat piece of metal with a sharp edge on the end of a handle.

words.ex: He picked up a spoon to eat the soup.
words.ex_cn: 他拿起一把勺子喝汤。
words.en: A spoon is an object used for eating, stirring, and serving food. It has a small shallow bowl on a handle.

words.ex: He eats rice with chopsticks.
words.ex_cn: 他用筷子吃米饭。
words.en: Chopsticks are a pair of thin sticks which are used to eat food, especially in East Asia.

words.ex: He wiped his mouth with a napkin.
words.ex_cn: 他用纸巾擦了擦嘴。
words.en: A napkin is a piece of cloth or paper used at meals to protect your clothes and to wipe your mouth and fingers.

words.ex: The doctor examined the tissue under a microscope.
words.ex_cn: 医生在显微镜下检查了组织。
words.en: Tissue is a group of cells that have a similar structure and that work together to perform a specific function.

words.ex: The tip of the pencil broke off.
words.ex_cn: 铅笔的尖端断了。
words.en: The end of a pointed or projecting object; a sum of money given to someone as a reward for their services; to give someone a small amount of money as a reward for their services.

words.tr:
n. 饮料；酒；
v. 喝；喝酒；
words.ex: I bought a cold drink at the store.
words.ex_cn: 我在商店买了一瓶冷饮。
words.en: To take liquid into the mouth and swallow it; a liquid that can be swallowed as refreshment or nourishment.

words.ex: He drinks a cold beverage after work.
words.ex_cn: 他下班后喝一杯冷饮。
words.en: A drink, especially one other than water; a liquid for drinking.

words.tr:
n. 水；
v. 给…浇水；给（某地）供水；
words.ex: She drinks water every morning.
words.ex_cn: 她每天早上喝水。
words.en: Water is a clear thin liquid that has no colour or taste when it is pure. It falls from clouds as rain and enters rivers and seas. All animals and plants need water in order to live.

words.ex: He drinks mineral water every day.
words.ex_cn: 他每天喝矿泉水。
words.en: Water that contains dissolved mineral salts, especially carbonates, sulfates, and phosphates of calcium, magnesium, sodium, and iron, and is often effervescent.

words.tr: adj. 已冷的； v. “chill”的过去式和过去分词；
words.ex: The chilled water tasted refreshing.
words.ex_cn: 冰凉的水喝起来很清爽。
words.en: If something is chilled, it has been made cold, often in order to make it more pleasant or refreshing.

words.tr: n. 含酒精的饮料；酒精；
words.ex: He drank alcohol at the party.
words.ex_cn: 他在派对上喝了含酒精的饮料。
words.en: Alcohol is a colourless liquid that can make you drunk, and which is used in medicines, cleaning products, and other substances.

words.ex: He drinks beer after work.
words.ex_cn: 他下班后喝啤酒。
words.en: Beer is an alcoholic drink made from grain.

words.ex: He drinks wine with dinner.
words.ex_cn: 他吃饭时喝葡萄酒。
words.en: An alcoholic drink made from fermented grape juice.

words.ex: He drinks a glass of milk every morning.
words.ex_cn: 他每天早上喝一杯牛奶。
words.en: Milk is a white liquid produced by cows, goats, and some other animals, which people drink and use in cooking.

words.ex: He drinks coffee every morning.
words.ex_cn: 他每天早上喝咖啡。
words.en: Coffee is a hot drink made from the roasted and ground seeds of a tropical shrub.

words.tr: phrase. 咖啡机；咖啡制造器
words.ex: He bought a new coffee maker last week.
words.ex_cn: 他上周买了一个新的咖啡机。
words.en: A coffee maker is a kitchen appliance used to brew coffee.

words.tr: phrase. 工作中的休息时间；茶歇
words.ex: We took a coffee break at 10 a.m.
words.ex_cn: 我们在上午10点休息喝咖啡。
words.en: A short period of rest from work during which people drink coffee or other beverages.

words.ex: He uses the coffee machine every morning.
words.ex_cn: 他每天早上都用咖啡机。
words.en: A coffee machine is a device used to brew coffee. It can range from a simple manual device to a complex automatic machine.

words.ex: He drinks orange juice every morning.
words.ex_cn: 他每天早上喝橙汁。
words.en: The liquid obtained from or present in fruit or vegetables.

words.ex: He drinks fruit juice every morning.
words.ex_cn: 他每天早上喝果汁。
words.en: A drink made from the liquid obtained from fruits.

words.ex: He drinks apple juice every morning.
words.ex_cn: 他每天早上喝苹果汁。
words.en: A drink made from the juice of apples.

words.ex: He drinks tea every morning.
words.ex_cn: 他每天早上喝茶。
words.en: Tea is a drink made by pouring boiling water onto the dried leaves of the tea bush. It is popular in many countries and is often served hot with milk and sugar.

words.ex: He drinks black tea every morning.
words.ex_cn: 他每天早上喝红茶。
words.en: Black tea is a type of tea that is more oxidized than oolong, green, and white teas. Black tea is generally stronger in flavor than the less oxidized teas.

words.tr: phrase. 黄茶（一种轻微发酵的中国茶）
words.ex: He drinks yellow tea every morning.
words.ex_cn: 他每天早上喝黄茶。
words.en: A type of Chinese tea that is lightly oxidized and has a mellow, smooth flavor.

words.tr: phrase. 高茶（英国传统的一餐，通常在傍晚食用，包含茶、面包、黄油、蛋糕和肉类等丰盛食物）
words.ex: She drinks tea and eats cakes at high tea.
words.ex_cn: 她在下午茶时喝茶吃蛋糕。
words.en: A light meal or snack taken in the late afternoon or early evening, typically with tea.

words.ex: I eat bread and eggs for breakfast.
words.ex_cn: 我早餐吃面包和鸡蛋。
words.en: The first meal of the day, usually eaten in the morning.

words.ex: I eat lunch at noon every day.
words.ex_cn: 我每天中午吃午餐。
words.en: A meal eaten in the middle of the day, typically one that is lighter or less formal than an evening meal.

words.ex: We eat supper at six o'clock.
words.ex_cn: 我们六点吃晚饭。
words.en: Supper is the last meal of the day, usually eaten in the evening.

words.tr: n. 早午餐（早午两餐并作一餐）
words.ex: We had brunch at a small café on Sunday.
words.ex_cn: 我们在周日去一家小咖啡馆吃早午餐。
words.en: Brunch is a meal that is eaten in the late morning. It is a combination of breakfast and lunch.

words.ex: He eats a burger for lunch.
words.ex_cn: 他午餐吃一个汉堡。
words.en: A burger is a flat round mass of minced meat or vegetables, which is fried and often eaten in a bread roll.

words.ex: He ordered a steak for dinner.
words.ex_cn: 他晚餐点了一份牛排。
words.en: A steak is a slice of meat, especially beef, that is cooked by grilling or frying.

words.tr:
n. 素食者；食草动物；
adj. 素食者的；素菜的；
words.ex: He is a vegetarian and doesn't eat meat.
words.ex_cn: 他是一名素食者，不吃肉。
words.en: A vegetarian is someone who does not eat meat or fish, and sometimes other animal products, especially for moral, religious, or health reasons.

words.tr: phrase. 素食餐厅；提供不含肉类及鱼类食品的餐饮场所
words.ex: We went to a vegetarian restaurant for dinner.
words.ex_cn: 我们去了一家素食餐厅吃晚饭。
words.en: A vegetarian restaurant is a type of restaurant that specializes in vegetarian cuisine, offering dishes that do not include meat or fish.

words.ex: He eats a sandwich for lunch.
words.ex_cn: 他午餐吃三明治。
words.en: A sandwich consists of two slices of bread with a layer of food such as cheese or meat between them.

words.ex: I ate an apple as a snack after school.
words.ex_cn: 我放学后吃了一个苹果当小吃。
words.en: A snack is a small amount of food that is eaten between meals.

words.ex: We had a snack and some drinks as refreshment after the meeting.
words.ex_cn: 会议结束后，我们吃了点心和喝了一些饮料作为茶点。
words.en: Refreshment refers to the act of refreshing or the state of being refreshed, especially by food or drink. It can also mean a light meal or drinks served in a social setting.

words.ex: He ate a piece of chocolate after dinner.
words.ex_cn: 他晚饭后吃了一块巧克力。
words.en: A food preparation in the form of a paste or solid block made from roasted and ground cacao seeds, typically sweetened.

words.ex: He ate a bar of chocolate after dinner.
words.ex_cn: 他晚饭后吃了一块巧克力。
words.en: A single, solid piece of chocolate, typically rectangular.

words.ex: He bought a loaf of bread from the bakery.
words.ex_cn: 他从面包店买了一条面包。
words.en: Bread is a food made from flour, water, and usually yeast, mixed together and baked.

words.ex: She spread butter on her toast.
words.ex_cn: 她在吐司上抹了黄油。
words.en: Butter is a pale yellow edible fatty substance made by churning cream and used as a spread or in cooking.

words.ex: He put the food on a clean dish.
words.ex_cn: 他把食物放在一个干净的盘子里。
words.en: A dish is a shallow container used for cooking or serving food.

words.tr: n. 比萨饼；披萨；意大利薄饼；
words.ex: I ate a pizza for dinner.
words.ex_cn: 我晚餐吃了一块比萨饼。
words.en: A pizza is a flat, round piece of dough baked with tomato, cheese, and sometimes other ingredients on top.

words.tr:
n. 鱼；鱼肉；
v. 钓鱼；捕鱼；
words.ex: He caught a big fish in the river.
words.ex_cn: 他在河里钓到了一条大鱼。
words.en: A fish is a creature that lives in water and has a tail and fins. Fish is also the flesh of a fish eaten as food.

words.ex: He eats cheese every morning.
words.ex_cn: 他每天早上吃奶酪。
words.en: Cheese is a food made from the pressed curds of milk, often with added flavorings and sometimes with a hard or soft texture.

words.ex: He eats meat every day.
words.ex_cn: 他每天吃肉。
words.en: Meat is the flesh of an animal that is eaten as food.

words.tr: n. 海产食物（如海鱼、贝类等）；
words.ex: We ate fresh seafood at the seaside restaurant.
words.ex_cn: 我们在海边的餐厅吃了新鲜的海产食物。
words.en: Seafood refers to fish and shellfish from the sea that are eaten as food.

words.ex: He eats eggs for protein.
words.ex_cn: 他吃鸡蛋来获取蛋白质。
words.en: Proteins are large, complex molecules that play many critical roles in the body. They are necessary for the structure, function, and regulation of the body's tissues and organs.

words.ex: She added a tomato to her salad.
words.ex_cn: 她往沙拉里加了一个西红柿。
words.en: A tomato is a soft, red fruit that is eaten raw or cooked as a vegetable.

words.ex: He ate a potato for lunch.
words.ex_cn: 他午餐吃了一个土豆。
words.en: A potato is a round vegetable that grows underground and has white flesh with a brown, red, or yellow skin.

words.ex: He eats a nut every morning for breakfast.
words.ex_cn: 他每天早上吃一颗坚果当早餐。
words.en: A nut is a fruit consisting of a hard or tough shell around an edible kernel. It is also a metal block with a threaded hole that is used with a bolt to fasten things together. Informally, it can refer to someone who is crazy or eccentric.

words.ex: The saltiness of the soup made it taste too strong.
words.ex_cn: 汤的咸味让它味道太重了。
words.en: The quality or state of being salty.

words.ex: The sweetness of the honey made her smile.
words.ex_cn: 蜂蜜的甜蜜让她露出了微笑。
words.en: The quality of being sweet.

words.ex: The coffee had a strong bitterness.
words.ex_cn: 这杯咖啡有很重的苦味。
words.en: Bitterness is the quality of having a sharp, pungent taste or of feeling angry and unhappy because of bad experiences.

words.ex: The sourness of the lemon made her face twist.
words.ex_cn: 柠檬的酸味让她皱起了脸。
words.en: The quality or state of being sour; acidity or bitterness in taste or character.

words.ex: The soup is too spicy for me.
words.ex_cn: 这汤对我来说太辣了。
words.en: Food that is spicy has a strong, hot flavor.

words.tr: phrase. 百货商店；百货公司
words.ex: She bought a dress at the department store.
words.ex_cn: 她在百货商店买了一条裙子。
words.en: A large shop divided into several different areas, each of which sells different types of goods.

words.ex: He goes to the mall to buy clothes.
words.ex_cn: 他去商场买衣服。
words.en: A mall is a large enclosed shopping area from which traffic is excluded.

words.tr: phrase. 商业区；大商场；大型购物中心
words.ex: We went to the shopping mall to buy clothes and eat dinner.
words.ex_cn: 我们去商业区买衣服和吃晚饭。
words.en: A shopping mall is a large building or group of buildings containing a variety of stores and often restaurants and other business establishments situated close together.

words.tr:
n. 商店；
v. 购物；
words.ex: I bought bread from the local shop.
words.ex_cn: 我从附近的商店买了面包。
words.en: A shop is a place where goods are sold; also, to shop means to visit shops in order to buy things.

words.ex: He enjoys window-shopping on weekends.
words.ex_cn: 他喜欢在周末逛橱窗。
words.en: The activity of looking at goods displayed in shop windows, especially without intending to buy anything.

words.ex: I buy milk and bread at the supermarket.
words.ex_cn: 我在超市买牛奶和面包。
words.en: A large self-service store selling foods and household goods.

words.ex: He saw an advertisement on TV.
words.ex_cn: 他在电视上看到一则广告。
words.en: An advertisement is a notice or announcement in a public medium promoting a product, service, or event or publicizing a job vacancy.

words.tr: n. 销售；出售；减价销售；
words.ex: The store has a big sale every winter.
words.ex_cn: 这家商店每年冬天都有大促销。
words.en: The exchange of a commodity for money; the action of selling something.

words.tr: 短语动词. 在出售；特价销售
words.ex: The shoes are on sale this week.
words.ex_cn: 这周鞋子在打折。
words.en: To be available for purchase at a reduced price.

words.ex: I found a great bargain at the market.
words.ex_cn: 我在市场上找到了一件便宜货。
words.en: A bargain is an agreement between two people or groups in which each promises to do something in exchange for something else. It can also refer to something bought or offered for sale much more cheaply than is usual or expected.

words.ex: The new policy is for the promotion of clean energy.
words.ex_cn: 这项新政策是为了促进清洁能源。
words.en: A promotion is a move to a more important job or rank in a company or organization.

words.tr:
n. 库存；股票；家畜；
v. 备有；贮存；
words.ex: The store has low stock of winter coats.
words.ex_cn: 这家商店的冬衣库存很少。
words.en: The supply of goods available for sale in a store; the capital raised by a company through the issue of shares.

words.tr: phrase. 缺货的；无现货的；已售罄的
words.ex: The store is out of stock of bread.
words.ex_cn: 商店的面包卖完了。
words.en: When a product is out of stock, it means that the product is not available for purchase because it has been sold out or is not currently in the inventory.

words.tr:
n. 折扣；
v. 不全信；不重视；
words.ex: The store gave a 20% discount on all shoes.
words.ex_cn: 商店对所有鞋子提供了20%的折扣。
words.en: A reduction in the usual price of something, or the act of reducing the price.

words.ex: The shop assistant helped me find the shoes.
words.ex_cn: 店员帮我找到了鞋子。
words.en: A shop assistant is a person whose job is to serve customers in a shop.

words.tr: n. 会员资格；全体会员；
words.ex: He paid $50 to get membership of the gym.
words.ex_cn: 他支付了50美元以获得健身房的会员资格。
words.en: Membership is the state of being a member of a group or organization.

words.ex: The customer bought a new phone.
words.ex_cn: 这位客户买了一部新手机。
words.en: A customer is someone who buys goods or services from a shop or business.

words.tr:
adj. 目前的；在场的；
n. 目前；礼物；
v. 呈现；提出；
words.ex: The present situation is very difficult.
words.ex_cn: 目前的形势非常困难。
words.en: If you say that someone is present at an event, you mean that they are there.

words.ex: She gave him a gift for his birthday.
words.ex_cn: 她送了他一份生日礼物。
words.en: A gift is something that you give someone as a present. It can also refer to a natural ability or talent.

words.tr:
conj. 直到；
prep. 直到；
words.ex: He waited till the rain stopped.
words.ex_cn: 他一直等到雨停。
words.en: Until a particular time or event.

words.tr:
n. 柜台；
v. 抵消；反驳；
adv. 相反地；
words.ex: The customer paid at the counter.
words.ex_cn: 顾客在柜台付款。
words.en: A counter is a long flat surface in a shop or bank on which customers are served. It can also refer to a device that counts something, or an action taken to oppose something.

words.ex: He kept the receipt for his new shoes.
words.ex_cn: 他保留了新鞋的收据。
words.en: A receipt is a piece of paper that you get from someone as proof that they have received money or goods from you.

words.ex: I asked for a refund after the product broke.
words.ex_cn: 产品坏了之后，我要求退款。
words.en: A refund is a sum of money that is returned to you, for example because you have paid too much or because you have returned goods to a shop.

words.ex: I buy apples at the market.
words.ex_cn: 我在市场买苹果。
words.en: To buy means to obtain something by paying money for it.

words.tr: phrase. 必买品；非买不可的东西；强烈推荐购买的商品
words.ex: This new gadget is a must buy for tech enthusiasts.
words.ex_cn: 这款新装置是科技爱好者必买的商品。
words.en: An item or service that is highly recommended or essential to purchase, often based on quality, necessity, or value.

words.ex: Water is a basic necessity for life.
words.ex_cn: 水是生命的基本必需品。
words.en: Something that is necessary or indispensable.

words.ex: She uses cosmetic cream to make her skin look better.
words.ex_cn: 她使用美容霜让皮肤看起来更好。
words.en: A cosmetic is a substance that you put on your face or body to improve its appearance.

words.tr: n. 一件物品或商品；项目；一则；
words.ex: This item is on sale for $5.
words.ex_cn: 这件商品正在促销，售价5美元。
words.en: An item is one of a collection or list of objects.

words.ex: She wears a silk dress to the party.
words.ex_cn: 她穿了一件丝绸连衣裙去参加派对。
words.en: A fine, strong, soft, lustrous fiber produced by silkworms in making cocoons and collected to make thread and fabric.

words.ex: She wore a dress made of cotton.
words.ex_cn: 她穿了一件棉质裙子。
words.en: Cotton is a plant that produces a soft fiber which is used to make cloth or thread. Cotton is also the cloth or thread that is made from this fiber.

words.ex: She knits a sweater from wool.
words.ex_cn: 她用羊毛织毛衣。
words.en: Wool is the hair that grows on sheep and some other animals, which is used to make clothes, blankets, etc.

words.ex: He bought a leather jacket for winter.
words.ex_cn: 他冬天买了一件皮夹克。
words.en: Leather is a material made from the skin of an animal by tanning or a similar process.

words.ex: The bird has a soft feather.
words.ex_cn: 这只鸟有一根柔软的羽毛。
words.en: One of the light, horny structures that form the principal covering of birds.

words.ex: The coat is made of soft fur.
words.ex_cn: 这件外套是由柔软的毛皮制成的。
words.en: The thick hair that covers the bodies of some animals, or the hair-covered skin(s) of animals, used in making clothes and other items.

words.ex: He hangs his clothes on the line to dry.
words.ex_cn: 他把衣服挂在绳子上晾干。
words.en: Clothes are the things that people wear, such as shirts, coats, trousers, and dresses.

words.ex: He wears old clothes to paint his house.
words.ex_cn: 他穿旧衣服来粉刷房子。
words.en: Clothes that are no longer new or fashionable, often considered to be worn out or outdated.

words.ex: He wears casual clothes to the park on weekends.
words.ex_cn: 他周末穿便服去公园。
words.en: Clothes designed for informal occasions, emphasizing comfort and ease of wear.

words.ex: He wears a white shirt to work.
words.ex_cn: 他穿一件白衬衫去上班。
words.en: A shirt is a piece of clothing for the upper body, typically having a collar, sleeves, and buttons down the front.

words.ex: He wears blue trousers to work.
words.ex_cn: 他上班穿蓝色的裤子。
words.en: Trousers are a piece of clothing that you wear over your body from the waist downwards, and that cover each leg separately.

words.ex: He left his slipper under the bed.
words.ex_cn: 他把拖鞋落在床下了。
words.en: A slipper is a kind of soft shoe that you wear at home.

words.ex: The pattern of the wallpaper is very simple.
words.ex_cn: 墙纸的图案非常简单。
words.en: A pattern is the repeated or regular way in which something happens or is done.

words.ex: The size of the box is too big for the shelf.
words.ex_cn: 这个盒子的大小对架子来说太大了。
words.en: The physical dimensions, proportions, magnitude, or extent of an object.

words.ex: He has a small dog.
words.ex_cn: 他有一只小狗。
words.en: If something is small, it is not large in size or amount.

words.tr:
n. 媒介；方法；
adj. 中等的；适中的；
words.ex: TV is a popular medium for advertising.
words.ex_cn: 电视是一种流行的广告媒介。
words.en: A medium is a method or way of expressing something.

words.ex: He has a large house.
words.ex_cn: 他有一所大房子。
words.en: Something that is large is greater in size than usual or average.

words.ex: She bought an extra large pizza for the party.
words.ex_cn: 她为聚会买了一个特大号的披萨。
words.en: Something that is extra large is larger than usual or larger than the standard size.
